Published online:
    August 31, 2026

Geographic focus:
    United States (with secondary focus on Middle East / Iran)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
    US equity futures sold off on Aug 31, 2026, driven by two compounding pressures: (1) renewed US-Iran military strikes disrupting Strait of Hormuz oil flows, pushing Brent crude up ~1.71% and reigniting inflation fears; and (2) newly appointed Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish debut at Jackson Hole, effectively ruling out near-term rate cuts. CME FedWatch shows >60% probability of a September rate hike, up sharply from 41.4% a week prior. All S&P 500 sectors except energy were under pressure. Key near-term catalyst: September 4 NFP report, which will heavily influence Fed's September meeting decision.

Q01. Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US market pricing?
Relevance: YES — directly covers Fed rate trajectory, inflation data, equity market pricing, and macro catalysts.

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 90 (strongly YES)
Probability of increase: 60%+ (per CME FedWatch as cited in article, up from 41.4% the prior week)

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 20 (marginally — holding is implicitly the prior baseline being displaced)
Probability of holding: ~40% (residual probability implied by FedWatch data cited)

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 5 (cuts explicitly taken "off the table" per Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks)
Probability of decrease: ~0% (near-term; Warsh's comments effectively eliminate this scenario)

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: 80 (Decidedly MORE hawkish than before — Warsh's Jackson Hole address marked a clear hawkish pivot for the new Fed chair, rate hike odds surged ~19pp in one week, cuts eliminated from near-term consideration, and geopolitical oil shock adds further inflationary pressure reinforcing the tightening bias)
